peopleAlsoAsk.question: Can dinoflagellates be cultured?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: One of the most impressive demonstrations of bioluminescence is also the easiest. Dinoflagellates, the most common sources of bioluminescence at the sea surface, are readily grown in the laboratory. They produce bright bioluminescence upon agitation.

peopleAlsoAsk.question: Where are dinoflagellates commonly found?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Dinoflagellates are common to abundant in both marine and freshwater environments. They are particularly diverse in the marine plankton where some cause "red tides" and other harmful blooms. More than 2,000 extant species have been described, only half of which are photosynthetic.

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What might be the adaptive significance of bioluminescence in a dinoflagellate?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet:
To startle predators (figure 13 (a))

 This first theory hypothesizes that dinoflagellates have developed bioluminescence to startle their predators (Hanley & Widder, 2017). As the flash of light shocks the predator, it provides enough time for the dinoflagellate to escape.
